content: The term chick can refer to several distinct topics: 1. In zoological terms, chick may denote: A chicken, scientifically known as Gallus gallus. A young bird, which historically originated as a dialectal variation of the word chicken. In the context of falconry, chick can specifically mean: A day-old male chicken, also referred to as a cockerel. A young bird of prey that is still in its fluffy, downy developmental stage. 2. The term chick may also be used as a reference to notable individuals, including: Harriette Chick (1875–1977), a British nutritionist recognized for her contributions to the field of nutrition science. Jack Chick (born 1924), an American publisher known for founding Chick Publications. Chick Hearn (1916–2002), an American sportscaster renowned for his work in basketball broadcasting. Chick Corea (1941–present), an acclaimed American jazz pianist and composer. Chick Webb (1905–1939), a prominent jazz drummer and bandleader. Chick, a 1990s one-hit-wonder musical band. Chick, a clothing line created by Nicky Hilton. Chick Young, a Scottish journalist specializing in football coverage. 3. The word chick also appears in various other contexts, though it would not independently serve as a direct reference to these topics: Chick flick, a colloquial term for films primarily targeted at or appealing to women. Chick-fil-A, a well-known fast-food restaurant chain. Chick lit, a modern literary genre focusing on themes relevant to women. Chickpea, an edible legume commonly used in cooking. Dixie Chicks, a country music group. The Hot Chick, a 2002 comedy film starring Rob Schneider. Grand Rapids Chicks, formerly known as the Milwaukee Chicks, a professional women's baseball team.
